items.stem: A team removes direct identifiers (name, email) from an analytics dataset but keeps precise timestamps, device model and ZIP code. Why is this still a privacy risk?

options.text: The remaining quasi-identifiers can be combined to re-identify individuals
options.rationale: Correct: combinations of quasi-identifiers often enable re-identification even without direct identifiers.

options.text: Removing direct identifiers always guarantees anonymity
options.rationale: That is the misconception; quasi-identifiers remain a risk.

options.text: Timestamps and device model are never personal data
options.rationale: These can be personal data, especially combined.

options.text: Encryption at rest makes re-identification impossible
options.rationale: Encryption protects stored data but does not address re-identification of released data.

items.explanation: Correct: combinations of quasi-identifiers often enable re-identification even without direct identifiers.

items.stem: Applying data minimisation to a new feature, which approach best reflects the principle?

options.text: Collect only the fields the feature actually needs and justify each
options.rationale: Correct: data minimisation means collecting only what is necessary for the stated purpose.

options.text: Collect everything now in case it is useful later
options.rationale: Collecting for undefined future use violates minimisation.

options.text: Collect extra data but promise to delete it eventually
options.rationale: Deferred deletion does not justify unnecessary collection.

options.text: Collect sensitive data to improve personalisation by default
options.rationale: Default sensitive-data collection is contrary to minimisation.

items.explanation: Correct: data minimisation means collecting only what is necessary for the stated purpose.

items.stem: A product embeds privacy by design. Which TWO practices are genuine privacy-by-design controls rather than security-only measures? (Select TWO)

options.text: Defaulting new accounts to the most privacy-protective settings
options.rationale: Correct: privacy-protective defaults are a core privacy-by-design practice.

options.text: Limiting collection and retention to the purpose at design time
options.rationale: Correct: purpose-bound collection and retention is privacy by design.

options.text: Adding a firewall at the network perimeter
options.rationale: A firewall is a security control, not specifically privacy by design.
Backup encryption is a security control and does not address collection or purpose.

options.text: Enabling verbose logging of all user activity
options.rationale: Expansive logging increases privacy risk, not protection.

items.explanation: Correct: privacy-protective defaults are a core privacy-by-design practice. Correct: purpose-bound collection and retention is privacy by design.
